tasks.short: Record progress against the goals on the care plan.

steps.what: Read measurable goals described in the treatment plan in the care dossier.
Monitor the client for progress on those goals.
Evaluate client progress according to those measurable goals.
Speak the progress she will record, in her own words.
Draft a progress note for the care dossier from words she will record.

loop.purpose: Draft a progress note using only the words she just spoke.
loop.input: The spoken progress from this visit, plus the goal id and goal text already on the treatment plan.
loop.output: A progress note draft with no sentence she did not speak.
loop.check: Every sentence is one she spoke. Flag suicide, violence, or abuse when those words are absent from what she spoke.
loop.stop: If she did not speak, or a risk line is not in her words, write nothing and she types the note herself.
loop.why_not_simpler: The note is free text tied to a goal. A fixed form cannot tell which sentence belongs to which goal.

steps.what: File progress note v1 in the care dossier.
Check progress note v1 in the care dossier against the goals and her words.

tasks.design: She still monitors the client and evaluates progress herself. {OTHER} drafts a progress note only from words she speaks, then files progress note v1 in the care dossier only after she checks that version against those words and the goals. It does not message the client, raise an alert, score a goal as met, or record the session.
tasks.previous_blocker: The progress note is free text tied to a goal. A fixed form cannot tell which sentence belongs to which goal, and a draft that adds a risk line she did not say is unsafe to file.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can draft only from words she just spoke, and a check can refuse any suicide, violence, or abuse line that is not in those words. That check is a small build.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see the client and judge the goal. Works-council consent for using her spoken words is not a coding task. Notes about mental health stay easy to over-summarise.
tasks.human_edge: Only she knows whether the client moved on that goal, and only she can say the note matches what she saw and said.

ambition.what: She records progress against each measurable goal on the day she sees the client, only when those goals are already on the plan.

tasks.altitude: She still monitors and evaluates. Note time goes to her words and to the check, while the second typing into the care dossier is the part that drops.

reach.task: Write the bedside observations from the shift the social worker did not see.
reach.learn: Which goal lines the nurse already stored, so a blank goal is left blank and the draft does not run.

evidence.claim: A named product turns spoken notes into a SOEP report or a letter in the care record, in elder care, disability care and GGZ.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation and the unrelated phrase fish fingers in generated notes.
A Wmo talk-summary pilot published no time figures. It was weaker on mental complaints and multiple problems than on mobility, and consultants kept their own notes, so little time was saved.
Health data is a special category, and an eligibility decision must not be based solely on automated processing.
Recording staff conversations needs works-council consent.
Where this note is part of a GGZ dossier, that dossier is kept for 20 years.
Model knowledge: in a mid-size European hospital the social worker still writes the progress note after she sees the client. This company has not measured that.

assumptions: Goal id, goal text, and measure already sit on the treatment and care plan. The producer is this social worker or the treating clinician in an earlier task. That capture is not counted as time saved here.
If the plan has no goal id and goal text, the draft and the file do not run, and she types the note herself inside the speak step.

The loop reads only the text she speaks in the speak step. It does not record the room. Until the works council has consented to turning those spoken words into a filed note, the draft and the file do not run. Consent time is not counted as saved.
The standing record is progress note v1, filed only after she checks that version. A rejection writes nothing. The check time sits in the check step and is not deducted again.
Re-speaking a rejected draft is about 0.4 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task. No client message, no ward alert, and no score that a goal is met.
unknowns: Whether measurable goals are stored as goal id, goal text, and measure, or only as prose.
Whether the works council has already consented to turning spoken progress into a filed note.
research_questions: Are goal id, goal text, and measure separate fields on the treatment plan in this hospital?
Has works-council consent for spoken progress notes already been given?

incremental.description: Re-speak a rejected draft so the note matches the words she said and the goal text already on the plan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the care plan has no measurable goal, or she writes a walk-in observation by hand, the draft and the file do not run, so the saving on those notes is zero. The high case is a week where most notes still need her to re-speak a rejected line.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find home and work impediments from interviews and records.

steps.what: List home and work lines on the patient records in the care dossier.
Review patient records in the care dossier for impediments the list does not hold.
Hold interviews on environmental impediments to client progress.
Identify which impediments block that patient progress.

tasks.design: {OTHER} lists address, household, and work lines already stored on the patient record. She still reviews the narrative and holds the interviews, and she identifies the impediments. It does not file an impediment note, send a referral, or raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The impediment sits in a conversation and in a narrative record. A stored address does not say that the home or the job is the barrier.
tasks.enabler_now: Address, who lives there, and work status are often already on the admission record. Showing those three lines is configuration of the care dossier.
tasks.still_hard: The interview and the call on which impediment matters stay with her. Blank admission fields are common, and then the list is empty.
tasks.human_edge: She hears what the patient will not put in a record, and she decides which barrier actually blocks progress.
tasks.altitude: The interview and the judgement stay as they are. She sees three stored lines before she reads the narrative, and she still makes the call herself.

reach.task: Visit the home the social worker has not walked through.
reach.learn: Which barriers show up only on a visit, so an empty address line is not treated as no impediment.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: home and work barriers are usually found by interview and by reading the record, not by a stored flag. This company has not measured that.
Health data is a special category, and an eligibility decision must not be based solely on automated processing.

assumptions: The list shows only address, who lives there, and work status. The producer is the admissions nurse, outside this task. That capture is not counted as time saved here.
If any of those three fields is blank, the list is empty and she reviews the narrative at the full remaining time of the review step.
Identifying the impediment is her judgement. This task does not file a note, send a referral, or raise an alert. Recording progress sits in the progress-note task.
About 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is a second look when a stored line is stale. The review and the interview stay at full time and are not deducted again.
unknowns: Whether address, who lives there, and work status are separate fields on the admission record.
research_questions: Which of address, household, and work status does the admissions nurse store as fields rather than prose?

incremental.description: Look up a home or work fact again when the stored admission line is blank or stale.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When address, household, or work status is blank, the list is empty and she reviews the full narrative, so the saving is zero. The high case is a week where those three fields are present on most records.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel clients in individual and group sessions.

steps.what: List who is booked for these individual or group sessions.
Counsel clients and patients in individual and group sessions so they overcome dependencies and adjust.

tasks.design: {CALENDAR} lists who is booked, the session kind, the time, and the room. She still counsels clients and patients in the room. It does not write a counseling script, record the session, file a note, or send anything.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counseling is a live conversation. A script or a recording would change the session, and there is almost no paperwork inside it.
tasks.enabler_now: The booking already holds the client name, whether the session is individual or group, the time, and the room. Listing that roster is configuration of the calendar.
tasks.still_hard: The session does not get shorter. Dependencies, illness, and how someone adjusts stay her work in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She paces the session, notices when someone needs a pause, and chooses the next thing to say.
tasks.altitude: The sessions stay hers. The roster only tells her who is booked, and she gains no decision right over the counseling.

reach.task: Lead a dependency group this social worker does not run.
reach.learn: Which session kinds that counselor books, so a blank booking is left blank rather than guessed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: individual and group counseling sessions are still led in the room. This company has not measured that.
Recording staff conversations needs works-council consent. This design does not record the session.
What is said in the session is health data and a special category.

assumptions: The roster shows only client name, session kind (individual or group), time, and room. The producer is whoever booked the session in a prior task, often the social worker herself or a planner. That booking is not counted as time saved here.
If the booking is blank, the roster step is skipped and she reads the paper diary inside the session step, which stays at full time.
The session is not recorded, no script is generated, no note is filed here, and nothing is sent. A progress note, when she writes one, sits in the progress-note task.
About 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is correcting a booking that shows the wrong room. The session time is not deducted.
unknowns: Who books the session in this hospital, and whether session kind is stored as individual or group.
research_questions: Is the session booking held on the calendar with client name, session kind, time, and room as separate fields?

incremental.description: Correct a booking line that shows the wrong room or the wrong session kind before she starts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Walk-in sessions with no booking skip the roster, and she reads the paper diary inside the session, so the saving is zero. The high case is a week where most sessions were booked ahead.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan discharge to home or another facility.

steps.what: Read the ward note in the care dossier for the discharge date.
Talk through discharge to home or the other facility.
Decide the destination, the services and the date for this discharge.
File discharge plan v1 in the care dossier.
Check discharge plan v1 in the care dossier against destination, services and date.
Send discharge plan v1 to the other facility or to home care.

tasks.design: She still talks with the patient and decides the destination, the services, and the date. {OTHER} files discharge plan v1 from only those fields, and {EMAIL} sends that same version to the other facility or to home care only after she checks it. It does not file through a government portal, write a medical order, or send a plan she has not checked.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan mixes a conversation, a clinical judgement, and a message to another organisation. Folding the send into the talk would put out a version nobody has checked.
tasks.enabler_now: Destination, services, and date are fields she can name. A template can file those fields, and a separate mail step can send only the checked version.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to agree the destination with the patient. A missing date or a missing address stops the file and the send. Whether the other facility accepts mail is outside her control.
tasks.human_edge: She judges whether home or the other facility is safe, and she does not send a plan the patient has not discussed.

ambition.what: She settles home versus the other facility before the patient leaves the ward, when the discharge date is already on the note.

tasks.altitude: She still chooses home or the other facility. Filing that choice and sending the checked version are separate from the conversation.

reach.task: Accept a patient into home care after the ward discharge.
reach.learn: Which address field that coordinator keeps, so a missing address stops the send.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: discharge planning in a mid-size hospital is still a conversation, a plan the social worker writes, and a message to the next organisation. This company has not measured that.
Health data is a special category, and an eligibility decision must not be based solely on automated processing.
Annex III covers eligibility for public assistance and services, including healthcare, by or for public authorities. This discharge plan does not make that eligibility decision.

assumptions: Expected discharge date and medical limits come from the ward physician's note, outside this task. If the date is missing she asks the ward nurse inside the read step, which stays at full time, and the file and the send do not run. Asking a colleague is not a send.

Destination (home or a named other facility), service names, and start date are named by the social worker in the decision step. If any is missing, the file and the send do not run and she writes the plan by hand.

The receiving address is a directory entry kept by a care-coordination clerk, outside this task. If it is missing, the send does not run. The phone call to ask for the address is the incremental time, not a cut to the talk.

The file writes only the fields she named and does not add clinical sentences. The send uses exactly discharge plan v1, after the check of that version. The check time sits in the check step and is not deducted again.
About 0.4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers that phone call and a rare rework when the date on the plan is wrong. No government portal and no medical discharge order.
unknowns: Whether the patient has agreed the plan can be sent to the receiving organisation.
Whether the other facility accepts the plan by mail.
Whether the expected discharge date is a date field on the ward note.
research_questions: Does the ward note store the expected discharge date as a date, separate from the physician's prose?
Who keeps the receiving organisation's mail address, and is the patient asked before that mail goes?

incremental.description: Phone the care-coordination clerk when the directory has no receiving address, and fix a plan whose date does not match the one she named.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the discharge date, the destination, or the receiving address is missing, she does not file or send and finishes by phone, so the saving is zero. The high case is a week where most discharges already have a date and a mail address.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still monitors, interviews, counsels, and decides the discharge herself. The week drops the retyping of a progress note and of a discharge plan she has already worded, and the sending of that checked plan.
skills_to_grow: Compare a drafted progress note with the words she actually spoke, including a risk line that was not in those words.
Name the discharge destination and the services before a plan is filed.
Know when a counseling session must stay unrecorded.
role.ambitious_version: She records progress against each measurable goal on the day she sees the client, when those goals are already on the plan, and she settles home versus the other facility before the patient leaves the ward, when the discharge date is already on the note. She does not let a draft choose an impediment, a session, or a destination, and she does not send a plan she has not checked.
